terms.gloss: an orbit (of a planet or satellite)
evidence: Sen. NQ 7.10.2: lūnāris illa orbita (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: First the rut a wheel leaves, a track (Cic. Att. 2.21.2, Lewis & Short); Seneca and the poem Aetna already use it of the moon’s circuit. In Cicero the planets move in their orbēs.

terms.gloss: a circle, the circuit of a heavenly body
evidence: Cic. Rep. 6.15: sīdera circulōs suōs orbēsque cōnficiunt (Lewis & Short)

sources: Lewis & Short: orbita · Lewis & Short: orbis
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency (printed page numbers): p. 354.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
